issues: fin/cli.py main and fin/server.py Handler._serve only catch UserError, so any other exception escapes. Examples are decimal.InvalidOperation from core.q on a large amount such as `txn add --posting A=1e30`, ValueError from add_months/add_days at the year-9999 edge, and sqlite3 errors: the CLI then prints a traceback and the HTTP client gets a dropped connection instead of a 500.

fin/cmd_reports.py balance_sheet does not compute retained_earnings as income minus expenses. It sets total_equity = assets − liabilities and makes retained earnings the leftover, so the identity always holds and any ledger or conversion inconsistency is hidden. trial_balance likewise pushes its rounding residue onto the largest account without saying so.

fin/core.py post_txn checks the balance on unrounded Decimals but stores fmt(amount), and only the caller txn_add_cmd rejects sub-cent amounts. recurring_add/recurring_run (and the blank-posting amount) can therefore store rounded postings that do not balance, while import_csv quietly rounds instead of rejecting.

fin/server.py turns JSON bodies back into CLI argv strings (`--posting=acct=amt`, `--line=a;b;c;d`) and parses them again with argparse, so an account containing '=' or a description containing ';' is mangled. It also rebuilds the parser and reloads the modules on every request.

Logic is duplicated or dead across modules: the budgets SCHEMA is defined in both cmd_bank.py and cmd_reports.py, `_name` exists in cmd_books.py and cmd_invoices.py with different stripping, core._rate is unused, and the comment in core.convert ('most recent rate wins, in whichever direction') contradicts what the code does.

Layers leak between modules: cmd_books.period_close_cmd calls cli.audit directly, cmd_invoices imports cli.Parser, cli.build_parser swallows ImportError for server, and load_modules checks whether the module files exist on disk. Reports also mix conversion dates: ledger converts at each posting's date, the other reports at the report date.
strengths: cli.run is the single place for transactions (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK), authorization and audit, so every command is atomic and audited the same way. SQL always uses parameters and money is stored as strings and handled as Decimal throughout.
Invoices and bills share one model (docs/doc_lines/doc_payments tables, plus _doc/_pay/_totals) with little duplication. Domain functions are short and clearly named.

The tests are thorough and organised by spec section. A fails() helper checks exit code 2, empty stdout and an unchanged database snapshot, each test uses its own temp DB, and edge cases such as zero-sum accounts, currency conversion and bad periods are covered. The harness helpers are duplicated across the test files, though.
